checkLimits: The manifest cannot summarise itself, so a hand edit to a derived figure in it is not detected by any rule: the
gate checks digests, ownership, coverage and status, and a number in a sentence is outside all four.
The stale-claims check reads documents, not evidence: `evidence/**`, `tests/**` and the changelog are excluded,
and so is everything after the ledger's dated entries, because those are records of what was true when written.
It matches fixed wordings in English and Chinese rather than meaning, so a claim phrased differently passes.
The dirty-tree rule covers `runtime-evidence*.json` only; the gated, regression and audit-ingest records carry no
such flag, and it reads the whole repository, so an unrelated service being edited during this task's capture
marks this task's evidence as dirty.

provenance.survey: The ownership policy already declared 15 services and 14 data owners, but the runtime did not match it: audit-service was a first-class runtime service absent from the Maven reactor, the toolchain baseline and every gate loop, and the ten owner outbox tables had drifted into four different shapes, none of which carried the claim machinery the event runtime contract requires.

reviewHistory.summary: P0 was zero: cross-tenant write blocking, DML-only credentials with 1142 denials, no cross-schema grants, 20 of 20 artifact digests, 58 checks reproduced and the gates and 1429 regression all green were independently confirmed. The findings were about accounting rather than missing work.

The four first-round P1 findings were confirmed closed: the reviewer independently re-ran 23 of 23 gated classes and recomputed 46 of 46 digests. One new P1 was raised, that the gated runner's pass criterion was the mvn exit code, which an entirely skipped class also satisfies, and which propagated into VERIFIED and a green gate. Ten P2 findings were raised as well.

The third round closed the second round's new P1 and seven of its ten P2 findings. It returned REWORK on three new P1 findings: a ledger exit-evidence item judged NOT_APPLICABLE with a hardcoded PASS standing in for it, three numbers in the canonical manifest that did not match their evidence, and drift during the review, since building workflow-service for M2-006 made the evidence package unable to rebuild itself at the commit it named. P0 remained zero and the review independently reproduced the core runtime facts: DML-only credentials refused with error 1142, cross-schema denial, the Redis ACL scoping, and the migration histories.

P0 remained zero and the core runtime facts were reproduced again. Four P1 findings: the ledger exit-evidence item for rollback and compensation was still NOT_APPLICABLE in results while the rollback evidence beside it reported PASS and config assigned the requirement here, so the manifest contradicted itself in three places; five prose figures in results and two in knownGaps disagreed with the figures the generator derived; reviewedRevision named a revision that could not reproduce the evidence it described; and the gated runner's discovery was limited by a hardcoded service list, so a class added under workflow-service was invisible while the coverage check reported PASS.

P0 remained zero, every artifact digest matched, and the three commands passed. Two P1 findings, both accepted. First, the gated figures in the manifest came from a run that predated workflow-service, because the runner named its output after the date and the generator read a hardcoded date, so re-running could only produce files nothing consumed; measured by the review as 30/25/43 against 31/26/46 in the committed evidence. Second, the requirement the ledger names as a rollback and compensation test was reported PASS on the strength of a drift-refusal check that performs no rollback, compensates no owner and writes none of the receipts the requirement names, which is a claim about a different property; the term had been redefined in a code comment. The remedy chosen was to reassign the requirement to P1R-M2-006 and change the ledger line to match, since that task owns Saga compensation, manual recovery and the receipt tables and has delivered them.

P0 remained zero and the core runtime facts were reproduced again. Three P1 findings: the reassignment of the rollback requirement had reached the ledger and the config while four other places still claimed this task delivered it and held it VERIFIED; the gated figures were stale again because two classes added under M2-006 during the review changed them; and the tenant production-class figure was six where the review counted nine, because same-package references were not counted. The review also mutated the gate open on three ownership channels.

P0 remained zero and all sixty-one artifacts matched. Three P1 findings: two of the five places carrying the reassignment still claimed the opposite and a code comment did too; the tenant figure had two incompatible numbers in circulation with a stated definition matching neither; and the review request claimed to be transcribed from the manifest while carrying different figures, a duplicated block and a stale round number. The review confirmed the three ownership channels it had mutated open now fail on their mutations, stated that the circularity of in-repository self-verification is not by itself a reason to rework, declined to block, and named the one thing genuinely missing: a machine-readable requirement list on the ledger line.

P0 remained zero and all sixty-two artifacts matched, with acceptance alignment, runtime evidence, digest integrity, tooling and provenance all passing. Four P1 findings: a harness comment still called the drift check the rollback evidence the ledger names and redefined compensation as the platform recovery path; the same file still printed the tenant figure as six where the measurement gives nine; the execution record pointed the retention requirement at P1R-M2-005 where the config and manifest say P1R-M6-008, while the manifest claimed that disagreement was gone; and the review request still carried sixty-one artifacts against sixty-two, four rounds against seven, four not-applicable entries against three, and an unduplicated block it claimed to have removed. Each was findable with one grep, which is the shape of every round so far.

P0 remained zero and the runtime facts were reproduced again on real MySQL and Redis. Five P1 findings: the review request still carried four not-applicable entries against three, a byte-identical duplicated block and an inconsistent round number; the execution record still claimed the rollback requirement was delivered and implemented here while naming P1R-M2-006 on the same line; the runtime evidence named a revision whose harness did not contain the text it had written, because it was produced on a dirty tree; the review history had no eighth round while the commit message and the review request both referenced it; and the stale-claims checker was structurally unable to fire on the shape it was written for, because its exemption was per file and the exempt files were exactly the ones carrying those sentences.

P0 remained zero and the runtime facts were reproduced again on real MySQL, Redis and audit-service. Four P1 findings: the execution record's first section still listed the rollback path as this task's exit evidence while the ledger and manifest say it was reassigned, which is the sibling of the ninth round's line in the same file; the stale-claims check was wired to nothing, with no package script, no CI step, no gate call, no test and no entry in the manifest artifacts, so the previous round's structural fix was a tool rather than a protection; the reviewed files kept changing during the review, five commits including two that touched the manifest, ledger, review request, trajectories and history the reviewer was reading; and the rollback evidence claimed sixty-two migrations were scanned with no destructive statement found, where the tree holds seventy-five and the two files that do contain DROP TABLE or DROP COLUMN are both iam-service's, which the scan had skipped because that service migrates itself.

P0 remained zero and the runtime facts were reproduced again on real MySQL and Redis; the digest, provenance and no-unrun-reference checks passed. Four P1 findings, all account-versus-reality: the reviewed revision moved during the review for the third round running, including a commit that rewrote the checker the manifest lists as an artifact; the trajectory registry claimed ten reviews and listed four, and the sentence that had correctly said nine was changed to "Ten", a word the checker's one-to-nine vocabulary could not see, so an alarm was silenced by choosing a word outside its range; the manifest rendered "undefined tests with undefined failures" because the regression record's keys were renamed when its producer moved into the repository and the reader was left on the old names; and the request document still said 1435 where the suite reports 1439 and still called itself the tenth round.

P0 remained zero and every runtime fact was reproduced again: real MySQL 1142 across schemas, Redis ACL namespaces, 63/63 digests matching on disk and against the sourceCommit blob, no skipped tests, and all three not-applicable owners matching the ledger line. Two P1 findings, both introduced by the previous round's own repairs: the tracked test that guards the stale-claims check mutates files in the real repository, so a concurrently running gate reads the test's intermediate state and reports a false failure, and one run left a file modified; and the narrowing-MODIFY pattern written as COLUMN? reads as "COL" plus an optional "UMN" and matches neither spelling, so the manifest's "0 of them contain one" was the empty set while content-service V3 line 25 is a MODIFY of exactly the kind it was meant to catch. The reviewer also corrected its own opening misreading of the digest count.

results.details: 14 owners provisioned; each can read its own schema; the 13 externally migrated owners are DML-only with DDL and ALTER denied by privilege (error 1142); SHOW GRANTS names no foreign schema.
Every owner was probed against three other owners and every read was denied; the exhaustive declaration check is the grant listing, which names only the owner schema.

Every owner the policy gives a Redis namespace was probed, 16 in total: 15 owner probes covering all 15 namespaced owners, of which 1 hold no database of their own (api-gateway), plus 1 policy-level check. Each resolved to exactly one ACL user scoped to its own namespace, able to write inside it and refused in another owner's. The requirement's second clause is covered separately: the business fact row counts in 14 owner tables were identical before, during and after Redis was stopped and restarted, so losing Redis cannot create or lose a business fact.

13 schemas have a p1r_schema_history whose version set matches the migration files; applying V1 into an empty scratch schema created all five expected tables; invalid SQL was rejected with no residue.

Delivered at the storage layer. 10 *TenantIsolationTest classes run against a real MySQL, each against its own owner's schema, writing and reading facts with a JdbcTemplate and asserting that a foreign tenant's rows are not returned; all 10 pass when run with their flags. MEASURED, WITH ITS DEFINITION, because the figure moves with the method: resolving each test's imported production classes together with the main classes in its own package, then looking for a construction of one of them, 9 of the 10 instantiate at least one production class and 1 do not (NotificationTenantIsolationTest). Counting any import from a service package instead gives 8; counting any reference including static calls gives more. So this is evidence about schema-level isolation, and it is not evidence that every service's request path enforces the same rule. The HTTP-level two-tenant negative is residual and needs the synthetic per-owner account P1R-M0-007 builds and P1R-M2-009 wires into CI.

13 *FlywayMigrationTest classes run emptyAndExistingDatabasesMigrateAndFailureRecovers against a real MySQL, one per service including audit-service, and all 13 pass. That is what makes the ledger's "including audit-service" phrasing true rather than an inference from version reconciliation.

Owned by P1R-M3-006: a projection rebuild appears in no part of the ledger line for P1R-M2-006, whose scope is Saga, compensation, scheduled jobs, manual recovery and audit ingest, while content cache invalidation belongs to P1R-M3-006.

Owned by P1R-M2-006, and the ledger line for this task was changed to match. The only check this task had was a drift-refusal test: it performs no rollback, compensates no owner and writes none of the owner, trace, audit and recovery receipts the requirement names, so reporting it PASS was a claim about a different property. The fifth review said so, and an earlier version of this entry had called it the evidence the ledger names on the strength of a comment that redefined compensation.

Owned by P1R-M6-008: it implements account deletion requests, the cooling-off period, withdrawal, cross-domain anonymisation and the final subject state, and P1R-M8-012 drills retention and deletion. That single owner is what config/p1r-m2-requirement-owners.v1.json records, so the earlier disagreement with the execution record is gone.
Redis was stopped (unhealthy) and restarted (healthy), and the row counts of 14 durable business tables were identical before, during and after.

The gateway contract schema identifier is 37 characters while both schema_version columns were VARCHAR(32). Because the receipt insert used INSERT IGNORE, MySQL truncated the value into a warning and stored a corrupted receipt while the fact insert failed outright. The widening is read from the migration that performs it, requiring both columns to reach VARCHAR(64). The endpoint behaviour is read from the tracked check `scripts/runtime/verify-audit-ingest.mjs`, which mints a short-lived RS256 token, ingests one event and replays it: first ingest accepted observed 202; replay is a duplicate observed 200; one receipt observed 1; one fact observed 1; schema identifier stored whole observed m2.gateway.security-audit.evidence.v1; column wide enough observed 64

P1R 1439/1439 with 0 failures and 1439 passing, read from evidence/p1r/m2/P1R-M2-004/regression.json; the full suite reports 1934 tests with 0 failures and 7 skipped or incomplete, read from the same record. The legacy B failures that were pre-existing are fixed and each fix strengthened the assertion rather than relaxing it. How many is NOT VERIFIED here: no tracked record counts them, so a figure is not given rather than repeated.

rollbackEvidence.details: Checked against the migration files rather than asserted, and the scope is stated because the figure moves with it: 62 migrations belong to the owners that are migrated externally, and those were scanned for DROP COLUMN, DROP TABLE, RENAME and MODIFY that sets a VARCHAR below a hundred characters, which is the shape this scan can actually see. 3 of them contain one. NOT SCANNED, and this is the part that changes the conclusion: iam-service migrates itself, so owner-manifest.mjs gives it a null migrationPath and the scan skips it. Its 13 migrations are the rest of the 75 in the tree, and 2 of them (V13__key_and_version_idempotency_request_hashes.sql, V5__create_self_owned_jwt_auth_schema.sql) do contain DROP TABLE or DROP COLUMN. The sentence above is therefore a claim about the externally migrated owners only, and an earlier version of it said "across the owners" and "0 contain one" without either qualifier, which the tenth review measured against the tree and found false. The files that block it are content-service/V3__complete_content_persistence_schema.sql (narrowing MODIFY); social-service/V2__add_moderation_appeals.sql (narrowing MODIFY); audit-service/V2__widen_audit_schema_version.sql (narrowing MODIFY).

Measured by the harness: with a recorded migration checksum corrupted, the reconcile runner for learner_service exited 2 and refused with "owner schema reconciliation failed: learner-service migration V1__create_learner_service_schema.sql changed after it was applied". The record was then repaired in a finally block, so a failed assertion cannot leave a false checksum behind, and the runner converged again with exit 0. The recorded checksum was confirmed restored afterwards: true. This is the migration-safety evidence, not rollback or compensation: that requirement is owned by P1R-M2-006 and this task reports it NOT_APPLICABLE. The drift-refusal check above is a real property but it performs no rollback and writes none of the receipts the requirement names, which the fifth review established and which the earlier wording of this sentence denied.

knownGaps: The tenant guard is delivered at the storage layer through 10 passing *TenantIsolationTest classes, each running against a real MySQL and its own owner's schema. They write with a JdbcTemplate rather than through a service repository. 9 of the 10 instantiate a production class, counted by resolving imported and same-package main classes together and 1 do not (NotificationTenantIsolationTest), and the classes do not all assert the same thing: most assert that a foreign tenant's rows are not returned, while at least one asserts only that a guarded column has no default and that the schema credential cannot write another owner's tables. So this is evidence about schema-level isolation, not about every service's request path, and the policy line asking for a server-derived TenantScope on a request path is not measured here. The HTTP-level two-tenant negative remains open and is handed to P1R-M2-009: it needs a synthetic per-owner account, which P1R-M0-007 builds and P1R-M2-009 wires into real CI. P1R-M2-009's ledger scope does not itself name tenant guard, so this is a residual gap recorded against this task rather than a reassignment of the requirement.

The per-service Redis namespaces and ACLs are provisioned and probed for every namespaced owner, but no domain service uses Redis yet: only api-gateway and the legacy core-api configure it, so for the 14 domain owners the namespace is a reserved allocation rather than an enforced boundary in a live path. The Redis default user is still reachable without a password, so the namespace boundary does not constrain an unauthenticated client; that is a property of the local container rather than of this task's ACLs, and it is registered here rather than left implicit.
The owner outbox tables now carry the contract shape, but only content-service has a publisher and a consumer; the other owners still append rows that nothing publishes.

Some provisioning owners were baselined from an existing schema rather than migrated from empty, so their migration history records what was already applied rather than a replay from scratch. How many is NOT VERIFIED: the reconcile output reports the state per owner but no tracked record counts them, so a figure is not given here rather than repeated from an earlier run. The empty-database drill is covered by the Flyway tests above rather than by those baselines.

p1r_schema_history, written by scripts/database/reconcile-owner-schemas.mjs, is authoritative for the 13 externally migrated owners and records the version and checksum the reconcile runner applied. flyway_schema_history belongs to the service that runs Flyway at startup, which is iam-service today, and to the service-owned tests. They are not interchangeable: the reconcile history is what the platform asserts, and a Flyway history exists only where a service or its tests actually ran Flyway.

The gated test families in this task are unchanged in themselves; what changed is that they are now run on purpose. A default `mvn test` still reports them as skipped, so any future evidence that cites them has to run scripts/runtime/run-gated-db-tests.mjs, which discovers 33 classes across the repository and reports the ones it could not run.

This task changed a value in the frozen D2 data-ownership policy and the assertion that enforced it in the same commit: the api-gateway Redis namespace moved from gateway to englishflow:gateway so that the policy, the ACL provisioning script and the running Gateway agree. It is registered here because changing a policy and the check that guards it together is a conflict of interest, and leaving it to the commit message is not a record. The evidence for the change is in the harness: a probe against the bare gateway namespace is refused by Redis while englishflow:gateway is accepted.

The workflow-service built under P1R-M2-006 is a provisioned owner, so the counts here include it: 14 owners in total and 13 externally migrated. Its schema, credential and migration are delivered by that task, and its tenant guard and gated coverage are not part of this snapshot, which is why the gated class count is 33 while the Flyway coverage check covers 13 services.

The Redis default user is still enabled without a password, so the namespace boundary this task provisions does not constrain a client that never authenticates. That is a property of the local container rather than of these ACLs, and it is recorded because a reader could otherwise take "per-service Redis namespaces" for a complete boundary.

The workflow-service delivered under that task holds the compensation executor, the two-person approval and the recovery receipts as CODE DELIVERED, EVIDENCE PACKAGE PENDING: that task is still PLANNED, has no manifest and no verdict, so the requirement is not verifiably delivered by anyone yet, and the ownership config says the same.

The workflow-service built under P1R-M2-006 is a provisioned owner, so this task's evidence describes 14 owners and its Redis loss check reads 14 tables including that service's. Its schema, credential, migration coverage and tenant guard are delivered by P1R-M2-006, not by this one, and that boundary is recorded in knownGaps rather than only here.
